name: MCP6562T-E_SN
title: MCP6561/1R/1U/2/4: single, dual and quad push-pull comparators for 1.8 V to 5.5 V supplies
summary: A family of CMOS comparators with a push-pull output that swings from rail to rail and drives CMOS or TTL logic. The inputs accept common-mode voltages 0.3 V past either rail at 5.5 V, and a few millivolts of built-in hysteresis keep the output from chattering on the part's own input noise. Each comparator draws about 100 µA and switches in 34 to 56 ns with 100 mV overdrive. The MCP6561, MCP6561R and MCP6561U are singles in SC70 or SOT-23 with three pinouts, the MCP6562 is a dual in SOIC-8 or MSOP-8, and the MCP6564 is a quad in SOIC-14 or TSSOP-14; MCP6562T-E/SN is the dual in SOIC-8 on tape and reel.
key_figures: tPHL 56 ns, tPLH 49 ns typ at VDD = 1.8 V; 34 ns and 47 ns at 5.5 V
VSS - 0.3 V to VDD + 0.3 V at VDD = 5.5 V
push-pull, VDD - 0.7 V min high, 0.6 V max low at 3 mA / 8 mA
4 MHz at 5.5 V, 2 MHz at 1.8 V

circuits.title: Typical application: inverting comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: The input signal drives the inverting input. R2 and R3 divide VDD to set a reference on the noninverting input, and RF from the output back to that node moves the reference with the output state, giving hysteresis. The output is a logic-level square wave.

circuits.title: AC and DC test circuit
circuits.description: The circuit the AC and DC characteristics are measured in. Two 200 kΩ resistors hold the noninverting input at VDD/2, the inverting input is driven by VIN = VSS, and the output is loaded by 200 kΩ to VDD, 200 kΩ to ground and 25 pF.

circuits.title: Protecting the analog inputs
circuits.description: Series resistors R1 and R2 limit the current any input can draw, including through the internal ESD diodes when an input is pulled below VSS. External diodes D1 and D2 clamp each input to VDD when it is driven above the supply; R1 and R2 also limit the current in them. R3 is feedback from the output to the inverting input. R1 and R2 are each sized so that the most negative expected input drives no more than 2 mA.
notes: R1 ≥ (VSS - minimum expected V1) / 2 mA; R2 ≥ (VSS - minimum expected V2) / 2 mA.
The diodes may instead go on the source side of R1 and R2; their current must then be limited some other way and the resistors act only as inrush limiters.

circuits.title: Noninverting comparator with hysteresis, single supply
circuits.description: A reference VREF sits on the inverting input. The input reaches the noninverting input through R1, and RF feeds the output back to the same node, so the trip points are VTLH and VTHL of the noninverting trip-point equations. Only two resistors are needed.

circuits.title: Inverting comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: The input drives the inverting input. R2 from VDD and R3 to ground set the reference on the noninverting input and RF from the output adds hysteresis. For the trip points R2 and R3 reduce to their Thevenin equivalent R23 from V23, giving VTHL and VTLH of the inverting trip-point equations.

circuits.title: Connecting an unused comparator of the MCP6564
circuits.description: One comparator of the quad that is not used has its inverting input tied to VDD and its noninverting input tied to VSS, with the output left open. Its output then does not toggle and cause crosstalk, and no extra parts are needed.

circuits.title: Precise inverting comparator
circuits.description: An MCP6291 op amp in an inverting gain stage around VREF (input resistor R1, feedback R2) amplifies the input before it reaches the comparator, whose inverting input also sits at VREF. The arrangement serves applications that need higher DC precision.

circuits.title: Windowed comparator
circuits.description: The two halves of an MCP6562 compare the input against an upper threshold VRT and a lower threshold VRB, and an AND gate combines the outputs. The gate output is logic 1 when the input lies between VRB and VRT, with VRT above VRB.

circuits.title: Bistable multivibrator
circuits.description: R1 from VREF and R2 from the output set a switching level with hysteresis on the noninverting input, while R3 charges and discharges C1 on the inverting input from the output. The circuit oscillates when VREF lies between VSS (ground) and VDD, and its duty cycle follows VREF.

where.TC1: linear temperature coefficient of hysteresis, 10 µV/°C typ
where.TC2: quadratic temperature coefficient of hysteresis, 0.3 µV/°C² typ

operation.text: Three differential pairs work side by side, one for low, one for middle and one for high input levels, so the common-mode range reaches 0.3 V beyond both rails with low offset across it. Offset is tested at VSS - 0.3 V and at VDD + 0.3 V. The inputs are high-impedance CMOS with picoampere bias current.

A fixed hysteresis is built in. It is sized to preserve offset precision while still exceeding the part's own input noise ENI, so that noise cannot make the output chatter. VOS is the average of the low-to-high and high-to-low input-referred trip points and VHYST is the gap between them.

ESD diodes on each input clamp it about one diode drop below VSS and also clamp excessive voltage above VDD; their breakdown lets normal operation through while shunting ESD events. The circuit around the part has to limit input current to the 2 mA rating. With the common-mode voltage below VSS a large current can flow out of an input, so high-impedance sources may need a narrower input range.
The output keeps the correct polarity when an input goes past either supply.
The output stage swings rail to rail and is CMOS and TTL compatible. Its drive limits shoot-through current between the supplies during transitions. It can drive heavy DC or capacitive loads.

Resistors from the output to the noninverting input add hysteresis and set the trip points freely. More hysteresis cuts chatter when an input passes the other slowly and keeps a system from switching too often (a thermostat, for instance); chatter also raises dynamic supply current.

VDD is 1.8 V to 5.5 V above VSS, and the other pins are normally between the two. In single-supply use VSS is ground. A 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF bypass capacitor within 2 mm of the VDD pin is needed for good edge rates; a bulk capacitor shared with analog parts within 100 mm is optional.
Logic-gate loads barely change propagation delay. Supply current rises with toggle frequency, more so with larger capacitive loads, and heavier loads slow the output edges and the propagation delay.

At low humidity about 10^12 Ω separates neighbouring traces, so 5 V across them leaks 5 pA, more than the 1 pA bias current at 25 °C. A guard ring driven at the sensitive pin's voltage reduces it. In the inverting circuit the ring goes to VIN+ (the reference, such as VDD/2 or ground) and VIN- reaches its pad inside the ring without touching it; in the noninverting circuit VIN+ is the guarded pin and the ring goes to VIN-.

Output and input traces need separating, as rail-to-rail output edges coupling into an input can make the output oscillate. In SC70 and SOT-23 the supply pin 2 lies between OUT (pin 1) and +IN. In the SOIC, MSOP and TSSOP duals and quads OUT and -IN are adjacent pins 1 and 2, and the output trace is run away from the input pins.
On an unused comparator of the MCP6564, VIN- goes to VDD and VIN+ to VSS. Its output then cannot toggle and cause crosstalk; the connection uses the fewest parts and draws minimal current.
